'''Kobe Levose Brown''' (born January 1, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Noblesville Boom]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]]. Brown was drafted at the end of the first round with the 30th pick by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].

==Early life and high school career==
Brown grew up in [[Huntsville, Alabama]] and attended [[Lee High School (Huntsville, Alabama)|Lee High School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rocketcitynow.com/article/sports/college/kobe-brown-talks-about-his-freshman-year-at-missouri/525-76fd41ef-9871-41a9-8e6c-2bcae8616665|title=Kobe Brown talks about his freshman year at Missouri|first=Mo|last=Carter|website=[[WZDX|RocketCityNow.com]]|date=April 2, 2020|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref> He averaged 20.9 points, 7.9 rebounds and 6.8 assists and was named first team All-State as a junior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/recruiting/2018/11/in-state-4-star-gf-kobe-brown-commits-to-sec-west-team.html|title=In-state 4-star G/F Kobe Brown signs with SEC team|first=Daniel|last=Boyette|website=[[AL.com]]|date=November 19, 2018|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref> Brown repeated as a first team All-State selection and was named the Huntsville Region Player of the Year after averaging 24.1 points, 12 rebounds and 8 assists per game during his senior season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/2019/03/i-just-had-to-suck-it-up-huntsville-player-of-the-year-kobe-browns-clutch-plays-while-sick-extended-lees-season.html|title=Huntsville Player of the Year Kobe Brown's clutch plays while sick extended Lee's season|first=Daniel|last=Boyette|website=[[AL.com]]|date=March 19, 2019|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref>

Brown was rated a four-star recruit and initially committed to play college basketball at Texas A&M during his junior year of high school.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/texas-am/Article/Texas-AM-basketball-recruiting-AM-lands-versatile-forward-in-Huntsville-Alabama-Kobe-Brown-124710083/|title=BREAKING: A&M basketball lands versatile forward in Kobe Brown|first=Damon|last=Sayles|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=November 14, 2018|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref> He decommitted as a senior and re-opened his recruitment.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/recruiting/2019/03/texas-am-signee-kobe-brown-of-lee-huntsville-reopens-recruitment.html|title=Texas A&M signee Kobe Brown of Lee-Huntsville reopens recruitment|first=Daniel|last=Boyette|website=[[AL.com]]|date=March 21, 2019|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref> Brown ultimately signed to play at Missouri over offers from Minnesota, Penn State and Vanderbilt.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schiffer |first=Alex |date=May 14, 2019 |title=Kobe Brown, 6-7 forward commits to Mizzou basketball |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/sec/university-of-missouri/article230400994.html |access-date=March 22, 2023 |website=[[The Kansas City Star]]}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Los Angeles Clippers (2023–2026)===
Brown was selected by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the first round of the [[2023 NBA draft]] with the 30th overall pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Clippers build depth by selecting Kobe Brown, Jordan Miller in NBA draft|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/story/2023-06-22/clippers-nba-draft-kobe-brown-jordan-miller|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 23, 2023|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi}}</ref> The [[2023 NBA Summer League]] boasted two players vying to be the second player to play in the NBA named Kobe (the other was [[Kobe Bufkin]]). Both were named after [[Kobe Bryant]], although this is debated by Bufkin's family.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kobe's NBA legacy lives on in new way|url=https://www.thescore.com/news/2676350|website=TheScore.com|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=July 12, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2024}}</ref> Brown debuted in the [[2023-24 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]]' first game of the season on October 25 against [[2023–24 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland]] without scoring in five minutes and 18 seconds of play.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kobe Brown 2023-24 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/brownko01/gamelog/2024|website=Basketball-Reference.com|publisher=[[Sports Reference]]|access-date=March 7, 2024}}</ref> Throughout his rookie and sophomore seasons, he has been [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|Ontario and San Diego Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Ontario Clippers Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Ontario-Clippers/65/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 29, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 San Diego Clippers Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/San-Diego-Clippers/69/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 29, 2024}}</ref> Brown made 44 appearances for Los Angeles during his rookie campaign, averaging 2.0 points, 1.4 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kobe Brown 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431752/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=April 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

Brown played in 40 contests for the Clippers during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], recording averages of 1.9 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kobe Brown 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431752/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=April 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> He made 34 appearances for Los Angeles in the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 2.9 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 0.8 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kobe Brown 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431752/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=April 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2026–present)===
On February 5, 2026, Brown and [[Ivica Zubac]] were traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for [[Bennedict Mathurin]], [[Isaiah Jackson (basketball)|Isaiah Jackson]], two first-round picks, and a second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-acquire-ivica-zubac-and-kobe-brown-from-los-angeles-clippers|title=Indiana Pacers Acquire Ivica Zubac and Kobe Brown from Los Angeles Clippers|work=NBA.com|date=5 February 2026|access-date=6 February 2026}}</ref> He made 27 appearances (including 10 starts) for Indiana, recording averages of 9.4 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 2.0 assists.

On July 10, 2026, Brown re–signed with the Pacers on a [[Two-way contract|two-way contract]], splitting time with the [[NBA G League|G League]]'s [[Noblesville Boom]].

==Personal life==
Brown's father, Greg Brown, was his coach at Lee High School and played collegiately at [[Athens State University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/sec/university-of-missouri/article255660816.html|title=Missouri Tigers basketball: Kobe and Kaleb Brown reunited|work=[[The Kansas City Star]]|date=November 11, 2021|access-date=July 20, 2023|last=Bromberg|first=Lila}}</ref> His younger brother, Kaleb, played basketball at Missouri and was his teammate for his final two seasons at the school.<ref>{{cite web |last=Stahl |first=Matt |date=January 21, 2023 |title=Kobe and Kaleb Brown will miss Alabama game |url=https://www.columbiatribune.com/story/sports/college/tiger-extra/2023/01/21/mizzou-basketball-kobe-and-kaleb-brown-will-miss-alabama-game/69829123007/ |access-date=July 20, 2023 |work=[[Columbia Daily Tribune]]}}</ref>
